findings.summary: crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The content rule takes its exclusion rules from the landing's parent, but the verified fingerprint was computed under the job base's rules.
findings.evidence: run.rs:1614 computes the verified fingerprint as `fingerprint(&self.git, &c, &p)`, where p is the job's base. land.rs:8-10 and :81 (`land::plan`) also use P, the job's base, as the rules source. Neither uses the landing commit's parent, so the plan's claim that it follows the same convention as `land::plan` is wrong. If a job's own work changes the exclusion rules, a legitimate PR would fail with a content mismatch. Fix: Use the job's base commit as the rules source, read from the landing's job/candidate records the same way the verifier does. Keep the landing parent only as a fallback, and say so in the doc entry.

findings.summary: No test runs the command to check its exit codes; criterion 5 is shown only by reading the diff.
findings.evidence: The plan shows exit 2 on failure and 0 on pass only by reading the diff. The CI job depends on that exit code, and the 'verified' default says user-facing behaviour is verified by exercising it. A CLI test directory already exists (crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs). Fix: Add a CLI-level test that runs `athena check --pr-head` on a failing fixture range and on a passing one, asserting exit 2 with the offending sha in the output, and exit 0.

findings.summary: `continue-on-error: true` hides the check's failures; leaving the job out of branch protection is already enough to keep it non-blocking.
findings.evidence: The job is already non-blocking because it is not in branch protection. `continue-on-error: true` also makes the workflow run report success when the check fails, so a maintainer can miss the failure, and the cutover in job 7 would then need two edits. Fix: Leave out `continue-on-error`. Rely on the job not being a required status, and say so in the comment. If the flag is kept, the comment should explain it and say job 7 removes it.

findings.summary: The workflow header comment still says 'Both jobs' and describes caching on every job.
findings.evidence: The header comment says 'Both jobs check out the full history and start with ./setup.sh --ci'. A third job makes 'Both' wrong, and the new job also skips the cache layers that the header describes as used by every run. Fix: Update the header comment to cover the third job and its lack of caching. This edits only the comment; the existing jobs stay unchanged.

findings.summary: `prediction_problem` takes a reading number, not the accepted reading itself.
findings.evidence: invariant.rs:648 is `fn prediction_problem(files: &JobFiles, job: &JobId, n: u32)`. It takes a reading number and the JobId, not a Reading. `accepted_reading` is an `Option<u32>`, so a missing value has to be handled before the call. Fix: State the call as `prediction_problem(&files, job, n)` with n from `job.accepted_reading`, and add a separate offence when `accepted_reading` is None. Step 4 already covers the None case.

summary: The plan fits the request and the reading, and the code it names exists. `land::pr_commits` (land.rs:145) bails on the first bad commit, so pulling the loop body out into `classify_commit` is the right place to make the check list every offending commit, and it leaves the classification rules alone. `prediction_problem` (invariant.rs:648) is the gate's existing prediction-order rule; making it pub and reusing it avoids drift, and athena-core already depends on athena-gate. Athena's own finding about touching invariant.rs is minor and justified by that reuse. The tests are real git fixtures, and the multi-offence test would fail under first-error behaviour. The CI job is additive and pull_request-only. The findings are all minor or nit: the content rule should take its exclusion rules from the job's base, as `land::plan` and the verifier do (run.rs:1614), not from the landing's parent; the exit-code contract should be tested at the CLI, not only read from the diff; `continue-on-error` hides failures the check exists to show; and the workflow header comment and the `prediction_problem` call shape need small fixes. No blocker or major finding, so the verdict is accept.
